title: Offline vs Online Recommender Evaluation
interviewAnswer: Offline ranking metrics measure historical predictive quality, but online experiments measure user/system impact. Historical logs are biased by the previous recommender, so offline gains do not guarantee online lift.
keyPoints: Use temporal splits and candidate consistency.
A/B tests capture behavior and feedback loops.
why: Offline vs Online Recommender Evaluation appears frequently in data-science work because it connects mathematical assumptions to practical decisions, diagnostics and failure modes.
deepDive: Offline ranking metrics measure historical predictive quality, but online experiments measure user/system impact. Historical logs are biased by the previous recommender, so offline gains do not guarantee online lift. Use temporal splits and candidate consistency. A/B tests capture behavior and feedback loops. A strong practitioner separates the modeling assumption from the estimation procedure, checks diagnostics rather than trusting a single score, and explains what would make the method inappropriate.
workedExample: An NDCG improvement may reduce diversity or increase latency; online guardrails reveal that trade-off.
commonMistakes: Applying the method without checking its assumptions or data-generating process.
Choosing it because it is familiar rather than comparing against an appropriate baseline.

production: In production, validate assumptions on real data, monitor the quantities that can drift, and keep a simple baseline so added complexity has a measurable reason to exist.
